title: Boeing Bent a 787's Wings Up 25 Feet to See If They Would Break

scenes.text: Engineers bent a jet's wings up twenty-five feet.
It was a Boeing 787 test wing, and they wanted to see if it would break.
They pushed it to 150 percent of the most extreme load it should ever feel.
The wingtips flexed upward about twenty-five feet.
The carbon-fiber wing bent that far and held together.
That's the strength behind the thin wings you see out your window.
So yes: twenty-five feet, and it didn't break.

description:

Boeing pushed a 787 test wing to 150 percent of the most extreme load it should ever see. The wingtips flexed about twenty-five feet and held.
Would you still fly after seeing that?
first_comment: Bonus: that test was meant to prove the wings could take more than any flight would ever demand. Would you trust a plane that doesn't flex?
